case_name: Arunachalam v P. S. R. Sadhanantham
respondent:
P. S. R. Sadhanantham
Supreme Court of India

6 March 1979
Criminal Appeal No. 170 of 1973.
The Judgment was delivered by : O. Chinnappa Reddy, J.
1. P. S. R. Sadhanantham and four
facts: P. S. R. Sadhanantham and four others were tried by the learned Sessions Judge, Tirunelveli, on various counts.
Sadhanantham (A1) was convicted under Sections 148 and 302 Indian Penal Code while the four others were convicted under Sections 147, 323 and 149 read with 323.
The first accused was sentenced to imprisonment for life on the charge of murder and to rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years on the charge under Section 148.
The others were sentenced to suffer imprisonment for a period of one year on each of the counts on which they were convicted, the sentences to run concurrently.
All the five accused preferred an appeal to the High Court of Madras.
The High Court allowed the appeal and acquitted all the accused of all the charges.
issues: Whether the acquittal by the High Court was proper
Whether the dying declarations were reliable
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution argued that the dying declarations were true and the evidence of the eye witnesses supported the case against the accused.
The prosecution also argued that the High Court had erred in rejecting the evidence of the direct witnesses.
respondent_arguments: The respondent/defending party argued that the acquittal by the High Court was proper as the dying declarations were not reliable and the evidence of the eye witnesses was not credible.
The respondent also argued that the High Court had correctly rejected the evidence of the direct witnesses.
court_reasoning: The court held that the High Court had erred in rejecting the evidence of the direct witnesses and that the dying declarations were reliable.
The court also held that the acquittal by the High Court was not proper as it was based on irrelevant grounds.
holding: The Supreme Court allowed the appeal and set aside the acquittal by the High Court, ordering a retrial.
cases_cited: See State of Madras v. Vaidyanath Iyer
